audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer read Skill on rows 0-5 while the content layer and packet levelChart read Karma / Karma / Karma / Karma / Anivia / Anivia / Anivia. Separately, the page called this EVEN at 5.5/10 against a 39.13% win rate over 46 games.
audit.why: Karma's early edge is real — Flash Frost is 11s and 80 mana at rank 1 and travels slowly enough to sidestep, so levels 1-5 belong to her. From 6 the lane inverts hard: Glacial Storm is a 4/3/2s toggle that doubles Frostbite inside it, Crystallize walls the exit on 17s, and Frostbite itself returns every 4 seconds. A 39% win rate is not an even matchup.
audit.corrected: Full-layer sides realigned to the content layer: Karma rows 0-3, Anivia rows 4-6, with each why rewritten to match. diff moved EVEN to TRICKY, diffRating 5.5/10 to 7/10, carry threat 6/10 to 7/10, and both copies of the rating sentence updated.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content whys were index-shifted, so whys[4] said "Level 5 is your last strong phase" on a row whose verdict is Anivia at Level 6 — the row argued with its own sentence.
audit.why: The phase labels are Level 1 / 2 / 3 / Levels 4-5 / Level 6 / First item / 2+ items. whys[3] described level 4 and whys[5] described level 6, both one slot late.
audit.corrected: whys[3], whys[4] and whys[5] rewritten onto their actual labels, with the level-6 spike carrying Glacial Storm and the first-item spike carrying the wall-stun-Frostbite chain.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single most important number in this lane never appeared: Frostbite is a flat 4-second cooldown, and it doubles against a target recently hit by Flash Frost or standing in a fully formed Glacial Storm. The range gap was also unstated.
audit.why: Riot's text on Frostbite: damage is doubled if the target was recently hit by Flash Frost or damaged by a fully formed Glacial Storm. Flash Frost is 1075 range against Karma's 950 Inner Flame, so once Anivia is itemised she pokes from outside Karma's answer.
audit.corrected: The doubling condition and the 4s cooldown are now in breakdown.cooldowns and enemyWin; the 1075-vs-950 range gap is in dontsFull[2].d and phases[0].why. breakdown.cooldowns previously contained no digit at all.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0].text said Rebirth makes "early kill pressure nearly impossible for her", which is backwards, and spikes[2].text called Karma's utility "melee-range".
audit.why: Rebirth reverts Anivia to an egg on fatal damage and she is reborn at full health, which makes killing Anivia cost two health bars — it says nothing about her own kill pressure. Karma's shortest ability is the 675 W tether; nothing in her kit is melee range.
audit.corrected: Rewrote both. spikes[0] now frames Rebirth as the reason to trade for tempo rather than kills; spikes[2] drops the melee claim.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ten fields called Anivia "he/his"; dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d were the tradeGood and tradeBad strings pasted under unrelated titles; dontsFull[1].d explained the W tether under a title about spending Mantra on waves.
audit.why: Anivia is she/her per champ-gender.js. Three bullet bodies answered a different question than their titles asked.
audit.corrected: All pronouns fixed; the three mismatched bodies rewritten to answer their own titles.

CONTENT whys[] INDEX DRIFT — THIRD OCCURRENCE. whys[4] read "Level 5 is your last strong phase" while win[4] read Anivia, so that row shipped arguing with itself. Same one-slot shift found on akali and akshan. This looks systemic across the karma content file rather than per-matchup; worth checking every karma matchup, not only the ones in this slice.

Unverified, so not asserted: whether Karma's W root can hold Anivia through the Rebirth egg transition, whether Frostbite's doubling window has a stated duration (Riot's text says only "recently hit"), and whether Crystallize can be walked through by any Karma tool — she has no dash, so I made no claim either way.
